name: SocialComponentServerFacet_SendAvailableTitlesToClient
summary: The client asks the server to send it the available titles. A 44-byte record with a 16-byte body - the shared head and NOTHING ELSE, so it is a bare request. Its name is the exact counterpart of 0x1033 SocialComponentClientFacet_ReceiveAvailableTitles, and the measured facet id is the same `ce81136a2b7ad33e`: the request and the answer are two members of one bus on one facet. The capture holds the request at seq 0x5f and the answer at seq 0x62, three records apart.
purpose: Ask for the title list. The answer is already modelled in this atlas: `0x1033` ReceiveAvailableTitles, a 494-byte body of two u32 vectors. That the two form a request/answer pair is a reading from the shared facet id and the paired names, NOT from a measured correlation - no request/response link between the two records was established from the capture.

created_when: the social component asks for its title list
lifecycle.if_absent: the client never receives its titles. The capture sends this at seq 0x5f and the 0x1033 answer at 0x62, so the request does precede the answer in this one session - but three intervening records make that ordering weak evidence on its own

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 af 40, i.e. type index 4143 = 0x102f. A client record carries the body at record offset 28: the 8-byte frame head and the 16-byte actor id precede the typed header, so a 16-byte body makes a 44-byte record.
